decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display stays close to the core cardboard offer and costs little to carry, but its absence from the website in 2020–2021 and the 2022 paper and energy cost squeeze raise pruning risk.
The pegboard-back display uses existing capacity and serves hook-merchandise clients, but rising input costs push management to review whether it meets aspirations, so the risk of a drop is moderate.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a staple format that fits the one-stop model and likely meets aspirations, so it is the least likely to be dropped.

The wooden pallet lies furthest from the cardboard core and has no visible evidence of success, and with slack shrinking under the 2022 cost pressure, problemistic search favours moving its resources back to the core and to new development.
Demand for media-product displays keeps declining structurally, and after the pandemic shift away from physical media the shortfall against aspiration justifies withdrawing it.
